newsitem.title: GERMANY: German union mulls UPS solidarity strikes.
newsitem.headline: German union mulls UPS solidarity strikes.

text.p: German transport union OeTV said it was considering calling strikes at United Parcel Service of America Inc German locations in solidarity with the Teamsters union strike in the U.S.
Union secretary Heinz Luksch told Reuters the OeTV was reviewing its legal position before deciding what action to take.

The union believed local action in support of the continuing Teamsters strike in the U.S. was justified since issues there such as part-time jobs and sub-contracting also affected Germany, although in different forms, he said.
"We are checking legally what forms of solidarity action are possible. We are thinking about solidarity strikes or a boycott," Luksch said.
But he declined to outline what precise measures could be taken at UPS sites in Germany, saying only they would be "things which hurt".
Possible action could include calling on other unions to pressurise German companies not to send parcels with UPS or disrupting airport handling, industry observers pointed out.

Luksch described a turnout of just 30-35 people at a union meeting on the UPS strike in Mainz on Wednesday night as "disappointing" but blamed this on good summer weather and little time to inform UPS workers of the event.
Michael Mensing, a Brussels-based UPS spokesman, told Reuters: "Solidarity strike action is illegal in Germany, there is no doubt about it. There is no legal way to do it."
He added: "If anything happened then we would consider legal action against anyone who is breaking the law."
The OeTV claimed to be representing UPS workers but even the UPS general works council in Germany had not been fully informed of the OeTV's actions, the company spokesman said.

UPS business in Europe was not affected by the Teamsters strike and service levels to and from the U.S. were being maintained by contingency plans, he stressed. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel +44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017 - www.racs.com
